items.title: NPL returns with bigger ambitions and global recognition
items.desc: The third season begins in Kirtipur on Monday with ICC recognition, DRS technology and greater scope for international players.

items.title: Houthi attacks raise safety fears among Nepali workers in Saudi Arabia
items.desc: Around 400,000 Nepalis work in Saudi Arabia. Recent attacks have raised fresh concerns about their safety as workers call for better protection and emergency arrangements.

items.title: Nepal opens door to private power traders, but legal hurdles remain
items.desc: The energy ministry has initiated the process of amending the Electricity Act, with a bill forwarded to the law ministry.

items.title: PHP Foundation ‘under-funded’ with one full-time staff member, director says
items.desc: Artificial intelligence has proved both a help and a burden to the foundation.

items.title: Two Japanese climbers found dead on Gangapurna
items.desc: Hidesuke Taneishi, 40, and Tetsu Hashimoto, 25, went missing at around 7,050 metres while climbing the 7,455-metre peak in Manang.

items.title: Nepali Congress falls short of one-third women’s quota in central committee
items.desc: All 69 women elected to the central committee won reserved or inclusion-category seats, leaving party president Gagan Thapa to nominate at least 30 more to meet the requirement.

items.title: Bay of Bengal cyclone could bring rain, snow to Nepal next week
items.desc: The weather system may affect Nepal from October 28 to November 1, prompting warnings for farmers to protect paddy crops and trekkers to exercise caution in the high Himalayas.

items.title: A look at the Prithvi Highway as Dashain draws to a close
items.desc: Vehicles carry people returning to Kathmandu after the Dashain break, while others travel to visit relatives after receiving tika and blessings.

items.title: Bhandari calls for long-term climate support for vulnerable countries
items.desc: Nepal’s former president Bidya Devi Bhandari urges Himalayan nations to cooperate on glacier monitoring and disaster preparedness, while calling for long-term international support for climate-vulnerable countries.

items.title: Rutherford, Hossain join NPL teams ahead of new season
items.desc: West Indies batter Sherfane Rutherford joins Sudurpaschim Royals after scoring 291 runs for Gujarat Titans in the 2025 IPL, while Bangladesh all-rounder Shamim Hossain signs for Lumbini Lions.

items.title: Seven killed as gunmen open fire at church in Jordan in 'terrorist' attack, authorities say
items.desc: Authorities blame extremists for the shooting during a funeral at a church in Karak, which also left 40 people wounded.

items.title: Modern night bus service begins between Jajarkot and Kathmandu
items.desc: Six buses are operating on the route, with fares set at Rs3,500 against the government rate of Rs4,066.

items.title: Road accidents in Kathmandu Valley fall during Dashain
items.desc: The number of crashes fell from 155 last year to 105 this year, while fatalities dropped from 10 to three, according to traffic police.

items.title: Ambani's Jio becomes most subscribed Indian IPO with $77 billion in bids
items.desc: The offering surpasses the 2008 Reliance Power IPO, attracting more than 13.8 million applications and drawing strong demand from institutional and retail investors.

items.title: David Miller joins Karnali Yaks for third NPL season
items.desc: The South African left-hander, a key player in Gujarat Titans’ 2022 IPL title win, brings extensive international and franchise T20 experience to Karnali’s squad.

items.title: Europe’s deadliest summer in 26 years leaves 50,000 dead, study estimates
items.desc: Scientists estimate that fossil fuel-driven climate change contributed to about two-thirds of heat-related deaths across 854 cities in 30 European countries.

items.title: Dashain brings fewer domestic tourists to Sauraha
items.desc: Hoteliers say fears of renewed road closures have kept visitors away, although international tourists are gradually returning after flood-related cancellations.

items.title: Kathmandu’s streets are filling up as Dashain winds down
items.desc: People are beginning to return to the Valley ahead of Dashain’s formal conclusion at Purnima, bringing more vehicles and pedestrians back onto the roads.

items.title: Rabi Lamichhane says India visit is personal, not political
items.desc: The RSP chair says he is travelling to fulfil a vow he made in prison, with visits planned to temples in Uttarakhand and Assam.

items.title: They never fought in the decade-long ‘People’s War’. They still bear its scars
items.desc: Civilians injured or disabled during the conflict, despite having no affiliation with either side, say the state has excluded them from relief and compensation programmes.

items.title: Wagle asks Jaishankar whether global cooperation is shifting towards ad hoc partnerships
items.desc: Nepal’s finance minister questions whether smaller, flexible groupings can replace traditional multilateral institutions or need stronger institutional backing.
